prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the exact same line in stdio_server() that sets the write_stream memory-object-stream buffer size (currently hardcoded to 0, i.e. a strict rendezvous channel with no slack). prs.title: fix(oauth): avoid lock contention for long-running requests
prs.author: ctaylor86
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock is held for the entire duration of the yielded HTTP request/response inside async_auth_flow, so a long-running request (e.g. an SSE GET stream) blocks every other concurrent request through the same OAuthClientProvider from acquiring the lock — the contention bug tracked by issue #2847. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock is held for the entire duration of the yielded HTTP request/response inside async_auth_flow, so a long-running request (e.g. an SSE GET stream) blocks every other concurrent request through the same OAuthClientProvider from acquiring the lock — the contention bug tracked by issue #2847. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: All three release the lock before the long-running yielded request instead of holding it for the whole response, and they edit the same lock-acquisition lines so only one can land cleanly. #3243 is the only one that also replaces `anyio.Lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` for both locks, with an explicit comment that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — `anyio.Lock` enforces same-task acquire/release and can raise when released from another task, a hazard #2858 and #3252 still carry since both keep plain `anyio.Lock` fields. #2858 is a rebase of an older community PR (#2660, closes #2847) and adds a second `refresh_lock` field for single-flight refresh semantics. #3252 has the smallest diff (no new lock fields) but still wraps the multi-yield full OAuth-flow code for the 401/403 branches in `async with self.context.lock`, so the same cross-task release risk remains there.

prs.title: Fix OAuthClientProvider._initialize() to enable transparent token refresh
prs.author: draesthetic
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, OAuthClientProvider reloads tokens/refresh_token from storage but never restores the in-memory token_expiry_time (and in some implementations the discovered oauth_metadata), so is_token_valid() treats an expired token as valid, the proactive refresh branch is skipped, and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent token refresh. (4 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, OAuthClientProvider reloads tokens/refresh_token from storage but never restores the in-memory token_expiry_time (and in some implementations the discovered oauth_metadata), so is_token_valid() treats an expired token as valid, the proactive refresh branch is skipped, and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent token refresh. (4 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 and #3251 make the identical change to `_initialize()` — computing `token_expiry_time` from the loaded token's `expires_in` via `update_token_expiry` — so they touch the same lines and can't both land. #3251 is a strict superset: it keeps that fix and additionally loads persisted `oauth_metadata` via a `getattr` duck-type check so `_refresh_token` can resolve the token endpoint without rediscovery. #2492 targets the same metadata-restoration goal but by adding two new methods (`get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata`) to the `TokenStorage` protocol, an interface change every custom storage implementation has to adopt; #3251's `getattr` check needs no protocol change and works against existing storages that never implement those methods. #2875 patches the same reported symptom only in the reactive post-401 branch, inserting a refresh attempt before full re-authorization, but never corrects `is_token_valid()` itself — so the pre-existing proactive-refresh check (before the request is even sent) stays broken and every restart still pays for a 401 round-trip that #3251's `_initialize()` fix avoids entirely.

clusters.pick_reason: #2654 changes the write_stream buffer size default from 0 to 1 directly, so the blocking-on-progress-notification bug is fixed for every caller with no code changes required downstream, and it ships a targeted regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact failure mode (slow stdout flush racing a queued response) before asserting the fix. #2215 only adds read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters defaulting to 0/0 - it leaves the default behavior (and the underlying blocking bug) completely unchanged unless a caller opts in by passing a non-zero size explicitly, and it touches a wider surface (both stream directions, public function signature) without adding a test that exercises the actual blocking scenario. members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py violates the MCP spec's cancellation semantics: when a request is cancelled, the responder currently sends an error response back to the caller. clusters.pick_reason: All three release the lock before the long-running yielded request instead of holding it for the whole response, and they edit the same lock-acquisition lines so only one can land cleanly. #3243 is the only one that also replaces `anyio.Lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` for both locks, with an explicit comment that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — `anyio.Lock` enforces same-task acquire/release and can raise when released from another task, a hazard #2858 and #3252 still carry since both keep plain `anyio.Lock` fields. #2858 is a rebase of an older community PR (#2660, closes #2847) and adds a second `refresh_lock` field for single-flight refresh semantics. #3252 has the smallest diff (no new lock fields) but still wraps the multi-yield full OAuth-flow code for the 401/403 branches in `async with self.context.lock`, so the same cross-task release risk remains there.

members.cluster_pick_reason: All three release the lock before the long-running yielded request instead of holding it for the whole response, and they edit the same lock-acquisition lines so only one can land cleanly. #3243 is the only one that also replaces `anyio.Lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` for both locks, with an explicit comment that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — `anyio.Lock` enforces same-task acquire/release and can raise when released from another task, a hazard #2858 and #3252 still carry since both keep plain `anyio.Lock` fields. #2858 is a rebase of an older community PR (#2660, closes #2847) and adds a second `refresh_lock` field for single-flight refresh semantics. #3252 has the smallest diff (no new lock fields) but still wraps the multi-yield full OAuth-flow code for the 401/403 branches in `async with self.context.lock`, so the same cross-task release risk remains there.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in the streamable-http client exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the failure is never surfaced to the pending request, so the caller hangs forever waiting on a response that will never arrive. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 is a small, targeted diff against the exact `_handle_reconnection` bail-out branch (already marked `# pragma: no cover` as a known gap) that sends a JSON-RPC error straight to the pending request, resolving the hang without disturbing the rest of the session. #3098 pursues raising a `StreamableHTTPError` instead, which requires adding a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to work around anyio wrapping it in an ExceptionGroup, plus an unrelated import change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`) — a larger, more invasive change to reach the same fix for the same failure path.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the identical block in RequestResponder.cancel() and would conflict on merge. #2493 only removes the erroneous error-response send (and correspondingly changes the server.py branch from 'suppress duplicate' to an early return), leaving no replacement notification for the timeout/caller-cancellation cases described in its own title lineage. #2514 additionally imports and constructs CancelledNotificationParams to actually emit the `notifications/cancelled` message on request timeout and caller-initiated cancellation, so the peer is still informed of cancellation rather than just going silent. #2514's diff also drops a `# pragma: no cover` on the entered-check, implying it added test coverage for that path. Because #2514 implements the full spec-required notification flow rather than just deleting the bad send, it supersedes #2493's narrower fix.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py violates the MCP spec's cancellation semantics: when a request is cancelled, the responder currently sends an error response back to the caller. Per spec, no response should be sent for a cancelled request; instead a `notifications/cancelled` notification should be emitted to inform the peer. Both PRs rewrite the same cancel() method (and the duplicate-response-suppression branch in server.py's _handle_request) to stop the improper response send.

clusters.pick_reason: All three release the lock before the long-running yielded request instead of holding it for the whole response, and they edit the same lock-acquisition lines so only one can land cleanly. #3243 is the only one that also replaces `anyio.Lock` with `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` for both locks, with an explicit comment that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — `anyio.Lock` enforces same-task acquire/release and can raise when released from another task, a hazard #2858 and #3252 still carry since both keep plain `anyio.Lock` fields. #2858 is a rebase of an older community PR (#2660, closes #2847) and adds a second `refresh_lock` field for single-flight refresh semantics. #3252 has the smallest diff (no new lock fields) but still wraps the multi-yield full OAuth-flow code for the 401/403 branches in `async with self.context.lock`, so the same cross-task release risk remains there.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` directly on `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids where one is the int 1 and the other is the string "1" (causing false-positive 409s or cross-wired responses) and does not guard against a string id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` ("_GET_stream") slot. #3221 replaces this with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes ids by type (`i:`/`s:`) to keep int and string ids distinct and to make collision with `GET_STREAM_KEY` structurally impossible, so it covers the same fix plus the edge cases #3063's implementation misses.
